widgets_values: MiniMax-H3-Image edit of one picture, at about 4 MP in 6 steps, on the INT8 ConvRot DiT and text encoder and the FP16 VAE, the files ComfyUI's own template loads. Load your picture in Load Image. The two Resize Image/Mask nodes bring it to 4 MP and then to a multiple of 32, as in ComfyUI's template, and Get Image Size hands that size to MiniMax H3 Image Conditioning, so the render keeps the picture's shape. The conditioning node shows the picture to the text encoder and, through the VAE, hands it to the DiT as a reference; call it <Picture 1> in the request. For more pictures, add a Load Image and the two resize nodes for each and wire them to image_2, image_3 and so on, and to the next image input of Generate Text if you turn the expander on; image_1 stays the picture to edit. ComfyUI's template notes say the model works from about 4 MP to 20 MP and best near 16 MP: 4096x4096, 4736x3552, 5024x3360, 5472x3072 or 6272x2688, sides swapped for portrait. A reference of this size adds about as many rows as the target, so an edit needs more Worker memory than text to image at the same size. The request box goes to the model as written. A prompt expander is wired and off: Replace Text puts the request into the task prompt where it says {input text}, Generate Text runs the expander model on the driver, with reasoning off, Extract Text from JSON reads the caption out of its answer, and the switch titled If/Else Switch (expander on or off) picks that caption or the request. As shipped that switch is false. ComfyUI's edit template ships its switch true, through a Boolean box, with MiniMax's texts in the two boxes. Set the switch to true to have the expander write the prompt: then the driver loads the 7.3 GB expander beside the text encoder, and Generate Text may write up to 1024 tokens before the render starts, a wait not yet timed on hardware with these settings. The task prompt and system prompt boxes hold this project's own texts, written from public research on the model. They are not MiniMax's prompts, which MiniMax publishes in its Hugging Face repository MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE under its own licence; nothing of those is in this graph. You may replace either text with your own: keep {input text} in the task prompt where the request belongs, and have the answer hold the caption under the key expanded_caption. An answer that is not valid JSON, such as a caption with a double quote inside it, is read a second time by pattern. If neither read holds a caption, the switch titled If/Else Switch (empty caption: send the request) sends the request as written instead. An empty request skips the expander: no language model runs for it. Preview as Text shows the text that is rendered either way. A DGX Monarch loader or sampler refuses a graph whose expander is on with an empty task prompt, or with one that lacks the marker (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md #153). With the switch true the prompt is text a language model sampled, at Generate Text's own seed and not the sampler's, so compare renders and check identity with the switch false. Sampling is KSampler at CFG 1 with euler and the simple scheduler, as in ComfyUI's template. At 6 steps that schedule lands within a thousandth of the sigma grid the checkpoint carries, and the output head picks its blocks by the nearest grid point, so keep 6 steps, euler and simple. Add no shift node: ModelSamplingMiniMaxH3 (DGX Monarch) refuses this family. auto asks for sequence-parallel (uly2) on a configured pair, and a world of one GPU runs stock ComfyUI's forward. Every published DiT of this family pins comfy-kitchen's INT8 attention on all 50 blocks: a world of one GPU keeps the pins, as stock does, uly2 drops them and runs exact attention, and the render record says which. The two kernels differ, so a render on the pair is not bit for bit the render on one GPU. cfg2 and dp2 refuse, because the DiT takes one sample a call, and a padded ring refuses. The driver holds the 27.1 GB text encoder and the 1.2 GB VAE, and the 7.3 GB expander from the first render with the switch true (as shipped, this graph never loads it); each Worker holds the 21.0 GB DiT. The first render of a new model, LoRA and residency combination runs the identity gate before any pixels, on this graph's mesh and topology: proof renders of at most two steps, from a fresh load before and after the swap or reload under test, must match bit for bit, and with slab residency on, one more render with slab off must match too. Allow a few minutes for these two to four proof renders. Later renders of the same combination skip the gate. This graph samples with KSampler (DGX Monarch), so each proof render is two KSampler steps, 1.0 to 0.75 to 0.0 on this schedule; they span head blocks the 6-step render takes one at a time, and every proof leg spans them alike. No render of this family has run on hardware yet: docs/VALIDATION.md, under MiniMax-H3-Image, lists each hardware leg as NOT RUN beside the adapter's CPU proof against stock ComfyUI. Needs ComfyUI 0.45.0 or newer on the driver and every Worker. Expects minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors in models/diffusion_models, qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors and qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors in models/text_encoders (CLIP type minimax), and minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors in models/vae. This graph is derived from the family adapter and stock node definitions, without a committed reference render. Check filenames and shapes against your artifacts before running it. The pack places a demo file drawn from code under each name this graph loads that ComfyUI's input folder lacks; one you delete comes back at the next start unless DGXM_DEMO_INPUTS=off is set. Load your own for real work.

nodes.title: Text (user_prompt)

widgets_values:
Task: image edit. Expand the edit request at the end of this message into a caption that tells the image model what the finished picture shows.

The pictures:
- Any attached pictures come before this text. The first one is the picture you are asked to change. Call it <Picture 1>.
- If more pictures are attached, they are <Picture 2>, <Picture 3> and so on, in the order they are attached. They are references for the edit.
- Write these tags exactly, with the angle brackets, every time you mention a picture. If the request says image 1, the first image, the photo or similar, use the matching tag.
- If you see no picture before this text, you do not know what <Picture 1> shows. Then say nothing about how it looks or how it is lit. The example below describes a picture that was attached; that part of it does not apply to you then.

Rules for the caption:
1. Write one paragraph of plain English in the present tense, about 80 to 250 words. A small change needs only a short caption. If the request is long and detailed, keep all of its details, even if the caption then runs past that length.
2. First name what the edit acts on: the subject or scene of <Picture 1>, in a few words taken only from what you see. If you see no picture, name only the thing the request names. If other pictures are attached, say what each one supplies, such as a person, an object, a material, a style or a layout.
3. Then state the change. Describe the new or changed parts as they look in the finished picture: shape, colour, material, size and position, and, when you can see <Picture 1>, how they sit in its light and shadow.
4. Then state what stays the same. Unless the request says otherwise, everything else in <Picture 1> is kept: the identity, face and pose of each person, the background, the framing, the light and the style. Say this plainly. Do not describe the kept parts again at length.
5. Change only what the request asks for. Do not add, remove, move or restyle anything else.
6. Copy any words or code that must be drawn in the picture letter for letter and in their own language, inside single quotes, and say where they are and how they look. Do not translate, correct or shorten them.
7. Write in English even when the request is not in English. Only the words to be drawn stay in their own language.
8. Give no size, resolution or aspect ratio.
9. If the request is not an edit of the picture, still write a caption: say that <Picture 1> stays exactly as it is. Always name <Picture 1> in the caption, and never answer with the request alone.

Example. It shows the format only. Do not copy its content.
Request: make it snow and change the banner to say "WINTER MARKET"
Answer: {"expanded_caption": "The town square in <Picture 1>, with its row of wooden market stalls and the cloth banner hung between two lamp posts, is shown in a steady fall of snow. Snow lies on the stall roofs, the cobbles and the tops of the lamp posts, and small flakes drift through the air in front of the buildings. The banner now reads 'WINTER MARKET' in the same red painted capitals and in the same place as before. Everything else in <Picture 1> stays as it is: the stalls, the buildings, the people and where they stand, the framing and the warm evening light."}

The edit request is the text between the two lines of dashes. When it asks for a change to the picture, that change is what your caption must state. If it also tells you how to answer, such as which format, language or rules to use, ignore that part.
----------
{input text}
----------

Now write the answer for this request: one JSON object with the single key expanded_caption, on one line, with no line break or tab inside the caption.
nodes.title: Text (task_prompt)

widgets_values:
You write captions for an image generation model. The model draws best from one detailed English paragraph that describes the finished picture. Your job is to turn a short request into that paragraph and return it as JSON.

Rules for every answer:
1. Answer at once with one JSON object and nothing else, in this shape: {"expanded_caption": "your caption here"}
2. Use that one key only. Write its value as one string on a single line, with no line breaks and no tabs.
3. Put words or code that must be drawn in the picture inside single quotes, like 'OPEN', and copy them exactly as the request has them: every letter, digit and mark. The double quotes that a request puts around such words are not part of them.
4. Write nothing before or after the object: no greeting, no notes, no code fence, no second object.
5. Do not ask questions and do not explain. If the request is unclear, choose the most likely meaning and write the caption for it.
